description: Measured reuse of the already selected latest row in miner comparisons.

source.change: Comparison passes its latest row to the existing window calculation through a shared helper. The summary wrapper retains its latest-row query; the read transaction, cutoff arithmetic, baseline fallback and ranking are preserved.

benchmark.method: Three alternating baseline/candidate pairs. Each value is elapsed batch time divided by 100 complete comparison calls. Full calls include schema initialization and connection cost; database construction is excluded. SQL tracing runs separately and is removed before timing.

results.interpretation: A modest 4.73% reduction in the median of three batch means, with all three pairs improving. The exact SELECT reduction is 96 to 64. Pairwise timing reductions vary from 1.58% to 19.62%; these measurements do not establish production or tail latency.

replay.working_tree: Use a dedicated checkout of measured_validation_commit with its parent Git object available; clone depth 2 is sufficient. The benchmark script is retained at that immutable commit rather than added to the original contribution.
replay.dependencies: Python 3.12 with stdlib sqlite3, Git, declared project dependencies requests>=2.34.2 and urllib3>=2.7.0, and pytest.
replay.sequencing: Run sequentially and stop if the existing tests fail.

limitations: One bounded, generated SQLite history; no captured live balances.
Three warmed alternating pairs of batch means, not a tail-latency distribution or a confidence interval.
No memory, cold-disk, live-node, or fleet-wide throughput measurement.
The benchmark and validation workflow remain on the immutable validation commit; this publication contains only the production source and this evidence.
